Trump has granted Ukraine licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles, says Zelenskyy

Ukraine had been seeking more Patriot interceptors to defend against Russian ballistic missile strikes, but the Iran war had depleted US stockpiles.

Ashwin Shekhar

26 September, 2026 10:01 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

US President Donald Trump and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York | Reuters file

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters in an audio message Friday that US President Donald Trump agreed to grant Ukraine a licence to manufacture Patriot missiles, ending months of uncertainty over the deal.

“There are concrete agreements in place… At our last meeting, President Trump emphasised to me that, ‘Yes, I have made a final decision. Ukraine will receive licences for the production of Patriot missiles,’” Zelenskyy said.

The MIM-104 Patriot is a mobile surface-to-air missile system developed by US weapons maker Raytheon to intercept aircraft, cruise missiles and tactical ballistic missiles. Ukraine has faced a shortage of Patriot interceptors, which are among the few systems capable of reliably countering Russia’s ballistic missiles. The shortage began in February, when the US-Iran war diverted Patriot missiles away from Ukraine.

Show Full Article

The licence covers domestic production of Patriot interceptor missiles, not entire battery ecosystems like radar arrays or launching stations. Ukraine will continue to rely on the US and European allies for those components.

The initial commitment from the US came in Ankara, Turkey, on 8 July during the 81st NATO summit. Trump discussed allowing Ukraine to produce the missiles domestically in response to concerns over supply, telling Zelenskyy to “make them yourself”. Asked about US defence contractors, Trump acknowledged they had not yet been informed but added that “they’ll be thrilled”.

The position was reversed on 31 July at Camp David during a cabinet meeting. Asked about the agreement, Trump said: “We have not agreed to that… We’re talking about it, but it’s a hard thing to give away that kind of technology… Nobody else has that capacity. These weapons are incredible. We have to be very careful about letting somebody build them… those people you give the technology, they could someday turn on you.”

Days later, Trump reiterated his position during a press briefing in the Oval Office, saying the US also needed to replenish its own missile stocks and pointing to the volume of ammunition supplied to Ukraine under former President Joe Biden.

“We want missiles too. Biden gave him so much, Biden gave $300 billion worth of ammunition,” Trump said.

In August, Zelenskyy launched a media campaign highlighting Ukraine’s depleted air defences. By early September, the US administration’s position had shifted to a cautious “maybe”.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said negotiations were “still ongoing” but cautioned that even after approval, establishing new production capacity could take several years.

The deadlock was broken at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, when Trump and Zelenskyy held a 40-minute meeting. Zelenskyy secured final authorisation directly from Trump, bringing months of uncertainty over the Patriot production deal to an end.

(Edited by Chingkheinganbi Mayengbam)

Iran will make no nuclear concessions, Iranian official says

Reuters

25 September, 2026 11:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Parisa Hafezi and Don Durfee UNITED NATIONS, Sept 25 (Reuters) – Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.

The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions are met” by the United States.

Under Iran’s proposal, Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Thursday.

Show Full Article

The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the US-Iran conflict, with Iran seeking relief from the US blockade that is choking its economy and Washington seeking free passage for ships on the global oil supply route now blocked by Tehran.

In a meeting with journalists on Thursday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he hoped a deal with Washington to end the hostilities could be reached before the US midterm elections on November 3.

Tehran said it would be prepared to engage in detailed negotiations over its nuclear program only after its conditions are met by the US.

But the official said Iran would give no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, one of the main US demands.

Israel, the United States and other Western states have long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, including pointing to its move to enrich uranium to 60%, far higher than needed for civilian uses and closer to the 90% needed for a weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons.

The International Atomic Energy Agency estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% when Israel and the US attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that has survived is unclear.

Iranian authorities have said that Iran could agree to dilute its most highly enriched uranium.

In May, Reuters reported that Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has issued a directive that the country’s HEU should not be sent abroad, according to two senior Iranian sources.

(Reporting by Parisa Hafezi; Editing by Howard Goller)

Text Size: A- A+

By Bo Erickson, Susan Heavey and Katharine Jackson WASHINGTON, Sept 25 (Reuters) – US President Donald Trump said on Friday he discussed the Iran war with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the US ambassador to China said Trump in White House talks made clear that Chinese help for Iran is unacceptable.

“We did,” Trump told reporters when asked whether he talked to Xi about Iran. “I think we’re going to do great.”

The US Ambassador to China David Perdue in a Friday CNBC interview said Trump reiterated to Xi that direct or indirect support for Iran was “totally unacceptable.”

Show Full Article

Asked separately on Fox News if that meant China would stop assisting Iran, Perdue said Washington received assurances from Beijing on Thursday.

“We’ve seen movement … on that already. That’s what the commitment is. They assured us yesterday they’re not doing that,” Perdue told Fox News’ “America’s Newsroom” program.

Trump and Xi did not take formal questions during the three-day state visit to Washington.

Earlier this month, Trump brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.

“They basically do what we do,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on September 13. “When they say China spies on us, I say you’re right and we spy on them too.”

(Reporting by Katharine Jackson, Susan Heavey and Bo Erickson; Editing by Peter Graff, Mark Porter and Chris Reese)

Can AI produce para-athletes? Finalists from AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha are among young innovators

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is a global initiative where students use technology to solve community challenges.

Sakshi Mehra

25 September, 2026 06:41 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File Photo | Kim Hong-Ji | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Eight young innovators from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha have reached the Top 20 of the Samsung Solve for Tomorrow 2026 competition. They bring five technology-based ideas aimed at improving para-sports, athlete performance, swimming safety and exercise support for people with Parkinson’s disease.

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is an innovation competition where students use STEM to solve community challenges. In its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

The eight innovators — Pasupuleti Ruthvik, Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla, Vatala Harika, Ritesh Routray, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, Jena R and Chriswin William D — are part of a national Top 20 cohort representing 18 cities across 12 states.

Show Full Article

More than half of the finalists come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, Samsung said. The Top 20 teams are now receiving mentorship and support to develop prototypes. Four winning teams will collectively receive Rs 2 crore in grants and incubation support from FITT-IIT Delhi.

Making swimming safer for visually impaired athletes Two of the five projects focus on challenges faced by visually impaired swimmers.

Pasupuleti Ruthvik, 21, from Chittoor developed Untethered, a wearable sensor system designed to alert swimmers when they are approaching the end of a pool lane.

For visually impaired swimmers, reaching the wall without a visual cue can be difficult and may result in head injuries. Ruthvik’s system provides real-time alerts, reducing dependence on manual cues from coaches and allowing swimmers to train more independently.

Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, 16, from Visakhapatnam, is working on a different challenge: maintaining direction inside the lane. His assistive trajectory system detects when a swimmer begins to move away from the intended path and provide real-time feedback, allowing the swimmer to correct their trajectory.

Also Read: Samsung turned first foldable iPhone launch into a roast. Apple fans are hitting back

Using AI to identify para-sport talent In Sundargarh, Vatala Harika, 21, and Ritesh Routray, 20, are using AI to identify para-athletes.

Their project, ParaSync, is an AI-based platform that assesses adaptive sporting techniques and identifies promising athletes. It also aims to connect them with professional coaching and competitive opportunities.

The project is based on the idea that sporting talent can emerge outside established sporting centres, where athletes may have fewer opportunities to access formal training and competition.

Wearables for safer exercise and training In Chennai, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, 21, Jena R, 20, and Chriswin William D, 20, are developing Rogue, a wearable device aimed at supporting exercise for people with Parkinson’s disease.

In Hyderabad, 21-year-old Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla is developing Somatrace, an IoT-enabled wearable designed to monitor spinal load among precision-sport athletes.

The device tracks movement and physical load in real time, helping athletes understand the strain their bodies experience during training and how they respond to different movements.

The eight innovators took part in a prototyping programme with FITT-IIT Delhi that included an Innovation Bootcamp and online mentoring from Samsung experts.

The programme helped them understand users’ needs, develop prototypes, identify potential markets, and understand the impact and scalability of their ideas.

They also visited Samsung Design Delhi, Samsung R&D Institute India facilities in Noida, Delhi, and Bengaluru, and Samsung’s headquarters in Gurugram.

Now in its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

Edited by Maryam Hassan
